method: Manual comparison of the two Analysis transcripts and three emitted L1 Systems with the exact behaviors/evidence delivered by js_context and the earlier source-grounded behavior review.

claims.claim: fetchApi copies caller headers and injects Comfy-User = this.user.
api.user is client-selected and persisted in localStorage Comfy.userId/userName, then populated only when the server user config exposes users.
The Comfy-User identity rides /prompt, /extensions and POST /upload/image.
claims.evidence: /prompt and /upload/image are supported by the delivered ranges; /extensions remains insufficient evidence in the earlier manual source review.

claims.claim: Header/localStorage identity is client-asserted and server-side validation is unverified.
claims.evidence: The model copied the unverified assumption rather than claiming server authorization.

claims.claim: All client traffic funnels through one fetchApi wrapper using api_base + /api + path.

claims.evidence: no-cache is the default, but a caller-supplied cache in the later spread can override it.

claims.claim: The wrapper handles multipart and JSON bodies.
claims.evidence: The delivered evidence proves a multipart FormData upload and JSON response parsing, not generic request-body handling.

claims.claim: The fetchApi wrapper accepts only HTTP 200 and otherwise emits a toast and throws.
claims.evidence: That behavior belongs to convertBlobToFileAndSubmit in audioService; the delivered fetchApi wrapper simply returns fetch and contains no status check.

claims.claim: The wrapper itself adds Comfy-User and no CSRF header.
claims.evidence: The wrapper adds Comfy-User to caller headers. The observation does not prove that callers never supply another header.

claims.claim: The hashed index chunk is the single SPA presentation asset and no HTML shell is mapped.
claims.evidence: This is true of the deliberately minimal replay graph, not a complete census of the historical target graph.

claims.claim: No L1Service exists, so no system_edges can be emitted.
claims.evidence: Preflight and graph census both showed zero L1Service nodes; the model did not invent one.

claims.claim: Client-side identity is not proof of server-side authorization.
claims.evidence: The transcript explicitly preserves the server validation gap.

assessment: The mechanism typist used the delivered behaviors in concrete L1 output and preserved several important uncertainty boundaries. It also inherited two weaknesses from the YAML and introduced one wrapper-wide overgeneralization about HTTP 200 handling. The output is useful as a refinement signal, not a fully source-correct architecture model.
